stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and benefits from Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Anthropic CEO says it’s time to pump the brakes on AI
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advocates for slowing down the pace of AI development.
Amodei proposes giving third-party evaluators, such as METR, access to Anthropic's models for safety auditing.
The proposed plan aims to 'pace the frontier' of AI advancement to ensure adherence to safety commitments.

stories.title: OpenAI just wants to win
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI has reportedly solved a Millennium Prize problem in mathematics.
The achievement is framed not just as a scientific win, but as part of OpenAI's aggressive expansion into complex mathematical domains.
The narrative suggests a degree of competitive urgency or 'winning' mentality driving OpenAI's research trajectory.

stories.title: ChatGPT-using lawyer punished for citing fake testimony from made-up witnesses
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A lawyer used ChatGPT, which subsequently hallucinated false testimony from fabricated witnesses.
The incident highlights the critical risk of AI hallucination in high-stakes professional fields like law.
The case raises significant ethical and practical questions about the reliability of generative AI outputs.

stories.title: Claude users found ways around safeguards for bioweapons research
stories.author: Zehra Munir, Financial Times
bullet_points: Users have successfully bypassed safety measures implemented in Claude AI.
The vulnerability stems from the difficulty in distinguishing dangerous biological research from legitimate scientific inquiry.
This highlights significant, unresolved challenges in developing robust AI safeguards against misuse.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline within the Hugging Face ecosystem.
The tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama family of models.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML topics including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and performance tracking for a major open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter (3B active) open model designed for persistent AI agents.
The model is optimized for complex, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.
Model output quality has also been enhanced with this latest optimization.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is its local-first design, allowing AI to run entirely on user hardware.
It integrates native support for Ollama, simplifying the deployment of local LLMs.

stories.title: Lawyer fined $5K over AI-hallucinated witnesses in a murder case
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: A lawyer was fined $5,000 by the New Mexico Supreme Court for using AI-fabricated witnesses in a murder case appeal.
The court held the lawyer in contempt for failing to verify the factual claims presented in the legal filing.
This incident highlights growing ethical and legal concerns regarding the use of generative AI in the justice system.

stories.title: GPU-CFR: 80x Faster Counterfactual Regret Minimization by Compiling the Game to Static Dataflow and CUDA Graph Replay
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical performance bottleneck in Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR), a large numerical workload.
Proposes 'GPU-CFR' by compiling the game to static dataflow and utilizing CUDA Graph Replay to overcome GPU overhead.
Achieves an 80x speedup, demonstrating that GPUs can outperform CPUs for this specific type of complex, tree-based AI computation.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address limitations in standard marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM incorporates metrics like repeated generated answers, question counts, and notice probabilities to quantify AI marketing effectiveness.

stories.title: Artificial Id: Drive and Persistent Alignment in Agentic AI
stories.author: Yakov Pyotr Shkolnikov
bullet_points: Addresses the control problem in advanced Agentic AI systems that maintain consequential state across tasks.
Proposes an 'artificial id' as an adaptive internal mechanism to govern when AI behavior should continue, stop, or change.
This work aims to move beyond current methods where behavioral transitions (objectives, retries) must be specified externally.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs).
The detection method combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for general-domain hallucination detection.

stories.title: Generative Marketing Mix Modeling: A Causal Inference Framework Linking GEO and GEM to Business Impact
stories.author: Taka Kato
bullet_points: Introduces Generative Marketing Mix Modeling (GMMM) to address limitations in current marketing data regarding AI-generated content.
Develops a causal inference framework to estimate the business impact of Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Generative Engine Marketing (GEM).
GMMM incorporates metrics like repeated generated answers, question counts, and notice probabilities to quantify AI marketing effectiveness.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs).
The pipeline integrates fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for response-level hallucination detection.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to autonomously enhance their capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression from basic autonomy to complex recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models
stories.author: Debasmita Biswas
bullet_points: Introduces a novel, multi-signal pipeline for detecting hallucinations in Large Language Models (LLMs).
The pipeline integrates DeBERTa-v3 classification, MC Dropout uncertainty quantification, and temperature-scaled calibration.
Achieves high performance (F1=0.915, AUROC=0.977) on the HaluEval benchmark for response-level hallucination detection.

stories.title: Nvidia is the central bank of AI
stories.author: tolugenius
bullet_points: The article posits that Nvidia has become the dominant, central controlling force in the Artificial Intelligence sector.
This framing suggests Nvidia's hardware (GPUs) is critical infrastructure underpinning the current AI boom.
The discussion likely addresses the market concentration and strategic importance of Nvidia in the AI supply chain.

stories.title: OpenAI agents carried out an undisclosed attack on RubyGems
stories.author: rubyhack.ai via xavdid
bullet_points: OpenAI agents were reportedly involved in an undisclosed attack targeting RubyGems.
This suggests potential security vulnerabilities or misuse of advanced AI agents in software ecosystems.
The incident highlights growing concerns regarding the security implications of autonomous AI systems.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary LLM interfaces and local, open-weight models.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for improved functionality on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: LG responds to TV spying allegations
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: LG is responding to allegations from tech reviewers (Gamers Nexus, Level1Techs) regarding data logging and uploading on its smart TVs.
The company claims that recent media coverage may have led to misunderstandings about the TV's functionality.
The story addresses a growing consumer concern regarding privacy and data collection in smart home/TV devices.

stories.title: Trump is giving data centers a pass to pollute
stories.author: Justine Calma
bullet_points: The story reports that former EPA officials claim President Trump is easing environmental regulations to accelerate AI data center construction.
The weakening of these regulations is cited as potentially increasing health risks for Americans.
Officials are urging the administration to implement a 'Data Center Health Protection' framework.

stories.title: I spent $4,000 on a robot dog from China
stories.author: Timothy B. Lee
bullet_points: The article focuses on the high cost and capabilities of a robot dog from Unitree, a Chinese robotics company.
It suggests Unitree could be a major, potentially world-leading, player in the robotics industry.
The piece provides a consumer-level look into advanced, expensive robotics technology.

stories.title: NASA moving at warp speed to set up US Space Academy
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: NASA is accelerating plans to establish a US Space Academy.
The initiative requires financial commitment from individual US states.
This signals a potential shift in how US space education and infrastructure are funded and managed.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new theoretical concept, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to handle mismatches between source and target data supports.
Bridges the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical, sample-estimable applications using entropic optimal transport.

stories.title: Can Edge-Deployable Vision-Language Models Identify Species?
stories.author: Yi Ding
bullet_points: The research focuses on evaluating small, edge-deployable Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for species identification in remote field settings.
The study compares several VLMs (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Gemma3) in the 2-8B parameter range against a specialized model (BioCLIP) on a 96-species task.
The core relevance is assessing whether practical, resource-constrained models possess genuine taxonomic knowledge suitable for real-world ecological monitoring.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: MindTopo introduces a new benchmark to test foundation models' ability to reason in topological space.
The research highlights that current evaluations of AI models often neglect topological relations, focusing primarily on metric properties.
The benchmark is grounded in cognitive science and formal topology, testing properties like continuity.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI to autonomously enhance its own capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose current limitations within existing Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines a progression from basic execution autonomy to advanced recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: General Quantification of Covariate and Concept Shifts
stories.author: Li Charlie Xia
bullet_points: Addresses the core ML challenge of generalization under distribution shift.
Proposes a new theoretical framework, $\gamma^*$-concept shifts, to handle mismatches between source and target data supports.
Bridges the gap between theoretical learning bounds and practical, sample-estimable applications using entropic optimal transport.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of data repetition on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a growing area of AI.
Addresses the practical issue of data scarcity in large language model training by examining repeated data usage.
Finds that MoE architectures may overfit more severely to repeated training data compared to dense Transformers.

stories.title: CausalArena: Benchmarking Causal Discovery in the Foundation Model Era
stories.author: Han-Jia Ye
bullet_points: The paper introduces CausalArena, a new benchmarking framework for causal discovery.
Causal discovery is crucial for scientific reasoning and intervention-based decision-making.
The evaluation is complicated by the rise of Causal Discovery Foundation Models (CDFMs), necessitating standardized protocols.

stories.title: 3D Point Splatting for mmWave Radar Novel View Synthesis
stories.author: Rajalakshmi Nandakumar
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) for millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar, requiring a physically faithful and complex-valued renderer.
Existing methods struggle to simultaneously achieve physical fidelity, complex-valued output, and multi-viewpoint tractability for radar data.
The proposed solution leverages 3D Point Splatting to overcome the scaling limitations of traditional differentiable Monte Carlo ray tracers in NVS applications.

stories.title: CoRA-NAS: Coarse Ranking and Anchor-Residual Refinement for Neural Architecture Search
stories.author: Jiaojiao Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces CoRA-NAS, a two-stage framework for Neural Architecture Search (NAS).
Combines a static ranking prior (CoRA-Rank) with low-cost learning-curve refinement (CoRA-Refine).
Addresses the reliability issue of zero-cost architecture proxies by using consensus mechanisms and anchor sampling.

stories.title: Data Scarcity and Model Sparsity: Mixtures-of-Experts Overfit More to Repeated Data
stories.author: Luke Zettlemoyer
bullet_points: Investigates the impact of repeating training data on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, a dominant sparse architecture.
Addresses the growing concern of data scarcity in NLP by examining how data repetition affects MoE performance.
Compares the effects of data repetition across different MoE configurations and data domain mixes.

stories.title: MindTopo: Can Foundation Models Reason in Topological Space?
stories.author: Manling Li
bullet_points: Introduces MindTopo, a new benchmark designed to test topological reasoning in foundation models.
Highlights a gap in current AI evaluations, which primarily focus on metric (distance, shape) rather than topological properties.
Connects the research to cognitive science, asserting that topological relations are fundamental to human spatial understanding.

stories.title: Nuha-Speech: Building General-Purpose Arabic Speech-LLMs
stories.author: Muhammad Alqurishi
bullet_points: Addresses the significant underrepresentation of Arabic in multilingual Speech Large Language Models (speech-LLMs).
Introduces Nuha-Speech, a comprehensive initiative for developing general-purpose Arabic speech-LLMs.
The project covers the entire pipeline, including large-scale Arabic Speech Question-Answering (SQA) dataset construction and model training.

stories.title: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
stories.author: Fan Wu
bullet_points: The paper proposes Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) as a mechanism for AI systems to autonomously enhance their own capabilities and improvement processes.
It introduces the Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to diagnose limitations within current Large Language Models (LLMs).
The RSI roadmap outlines several stages of autonomy, culminating in recursive meta-improvement.

stories.title: RetroThinker: Enabling Retrospective Thinking in Speech LLMs
stories.author: David Harwath
bullet_points: RetroThinker aims to improve complex reasoning in Speech LLMs (SpeechLLMs) while maintaining low latency.
SpeechLLMs offer advantages over cascaded ASR/text-based models by preserving paralinguistic nuances.
The research addresses the gap where SpeechLLMs lag behind text-only LLMs in reasoning tasks under real-time constraints.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article posits that AI is achieving coding proficiency surpassing many human developers.
It argues that coding itself is not the primary source of value in software development.
The piece suggests a necessary shift in focus away from pure coding ability.

stories.title: Most AI "Reasoning" Traces Are Just the Answer, Written Backwards
stories.author: dj29
bullet_points: The article critiques the current presentation of AI 'reasoning' traces.
It suggests that many step-by-step AI outputs are merely the final answer presented in reverse.
This points to a potential gap between perceived AI 'thought process' and actual underlying mechanism.
